title: Evidence-led speech cleanup
intent: Tighten spoken material without destroying speaker identity or conversational rhythm.
applicability: At least one source contains intelligible speech
Silence or transcript evidence is available
contraindications: Pauses are the central dramatic device
The source timing or transcript is unreviewable
rules: Keep conservative padding around measured speech
Link picture and speech unless an explicit J/L-cut is justified
Treat transcript and diarization as correctable evidence
heuristics: Prefer fewer natural cuts to maximal silence removal
Use reviewed transcript segments for captions
Use gain keyframes for evidence-authored ducking envelopes
constraints: Never remove a region solely because ASR confidence is low
failure_modes: Silence detector mistakes dramatic pauses for dead air
positive_examples: A talking-head recording with long setup pauses
An interview shortened with reviewed captions
negative_examples: A performance where breath and silence are intentional
Unreviewed multilingual speech used as automatic cut authority
promotion_questions: How should repeated phrases be ranked across languages?
Which J/L-cut defaults remain natural across interview styles?
What transcript review threshold is safe for caption export?
